column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has pardoned for me my nation their mistakes, their forgetfulness and what they are coerced into.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by Ibn Mājah, al-Bayhaqī and others.

The nation of our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ is of two kinds: the nation of invitation and the nation of response. The nation of invitation is every human and jinn from the time he was sent until the Hour is established;

the nation of response is those whom Allah has enabled to enter His pure religion and who have become Muslims. What is meant by the nation in this hadith is the nation of response. An example of the nation of invitation is found in the Prophet's words ﷺ: “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad,
no one of this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and then dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire.” Reported by Muslim (153).

A mistake (khaṭaʾ) is doing something without intending it; forgetfulness (nisyān) is remembering something and then forgetting it at the time of acting; and coercion (ikrāh) is being forced into a word or deed. The sin is lifted in these three.

The Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, contains proofs that it is lifted. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “Our Lord, do not take us to account if we forget or make a mistake” [al-Baqarah 2:286],
and Allah said: “I have done so” (recorded by Muslim, 126); He said: “And there is no blame upon you for what you have done by mistake, but [only for] what your hearts intended” [al-Aḥzāb 33:5];

and He said: “…except one who is coerced while his heart is at rest in faith; but [the one] who opens his breast to disbelief…” [al-Naḥl 16:106]. As for what he destroys of others' property, he is liable for it; for example, accidental killing requires blood money along with expiation. And if he is coerced into fornication or into killing an inviolable person, that is not permissible for him,
for he may not preserve his own life by killing someone else.
The hadith shows the vastness of Allah's mercy, favour and kindness to His servants,
since He has lifted the sin from them in these three.
Accountability for mistakes is lifted; but if the mistake was in leaving an obligation, he must do it, and if it was in destroying someone else's right, he is liable for it.
